stem:
The figure shows two length tools Farhan's class considers for measuring the same classroom board: a metre scale and one student's handspan. Someone also names the centimetre as the SI unit of length.

Which claim correctly decides whether a length unit is suitable as a standard unit?

options.text: The SI unit of length is the centimetre.
The metre is suitable as a shared standard length unit.
Each student's own handspan is a standard length unit.
The centimetre is not a standard length unit at all.

teacher.key_rationale: A standard length unit is shared so different people get the same measurement. The metre is that SI unit. Handspan varies by person; centimetre is a standard unit but is not the SI unit of length.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source force diagram into a metre scale beside a handspan mark.
